fill.Title: What moves the energy bill
fill.Subtitle: Home energy for non-specialists: where the money goes and what to do first

fill.Number caption: of a typical household's energy goes to heating and hot water
fill.Title: Heating is the bill
fill.Body: Any plan that does not touch heating and hot water only works on the remaining third. Start there.

fill.Title: Three levers, very different paybacks
fill.Subtitle: What each option does and when it pays back
fill.Body 1: Loft insulation usually pays back in 3 to 5 years. New windows take far longer.
fill.Body 2: Roughly three times less heating energy than resistance heating, provided the house is well insulated.
fill.Body 3: Help most when power is used during the day. A battery rarely pays back on its own.

fill.Title: Insulate first, then electrify heating, then add solar
fill.Argument 1 detail: It is the cheapest kilowatt-hour: the one you no longer need.
fill.Argument 2: Heat pumps need insulation to shine
fill.Argument 2 detail: In a leaky house the heat pump is oversized and runs less efficiently.
fill.Argument 3 detail: Size it to daytime use once heating is electric.

fill.Title: Three quick wins cost almost nothing
fill.Band 1 body: The easiest saving: no purchase, no works.
fill.Band 2 body: Doors, windows and loft hatch: seal what you can feel.
fill.Band 3 body: Use switchable power strips for TV and office equipment.

fill.Title: Six months from audit to heat pump
fill.Subtitle: Review after the first winter

fill.Point 1: Heating and hot water are two thirds of the bill
fill.Point 2: Insulation first: it pays back in 3 to 5 years
fill.Point 3: Then a heat pump, then solar sized to daytime use
fill.Point 4: Quick wins start this week, at no cost
